markdown_report:
At 10% research progress, prioritize a controlled diagnostic extension before changing HSTU training. No measured results establish the proposed mechanism yet.

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Deletion changes content and occupied positions. Fixed-slot replacements preserve positions but introduce replacement-distribution effects. (2) Final-event removal changes readout context. Preserving that event improves comparability without isolating internal mechanisms. (3) Feedback motivates testing historical dependence. It cannot establish ownership, satisfied needs, or intent.

**Related-work insights.** (1) HSTU combines attention, gating, and relative biases [1]. Input interventions probe their combined behavior. (2) Recency dependence can itself be excessive [2]. Recent and older interventions both require controls. (3) Sampled rankings can disagree with full-catalog rankings [3]. Shared candidates improve pairing without removing sampling bias. (4) Replacement choices can distort importance estimates [5]. Plausibility checks and coverage reporting are necessary.

Three research directions follow: controlled history sensitivity, component attribution, and evidence-aware interpretation.

| Direction | Existing approach | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| History sensitivity | Deletion, shuffle, replacement | Content and corruption effects remain entangled |
| Component attribution | Frozen gate/bias ablation | Hooks unavailable; activation shifts complicate interpretation |
| Interpretation | Functional relation annotation [4] | Titles cannot establish satisfied needs |

Three atomic ideas remain feasible. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Matched fixed-slot replacement: 5/7/5.** Originality: useful control synthesis, although perturbation methods exist. Potential: screens training hypotheses, although matching limits coverage. Difficulty: existing hooks suffice, although reproducible matching and uncertainty require care.
- **Frozen gate neutralization: 4/6/6.** Originality: HSTU-specific application, although ablation is standard. Potential: localizes sensitivity, although frozen interventions cannot predict retraining benefits. Difficulty: concise with hooks, although internals are unspecified.
- **Evidence-backed relation audit: 5/7/7.** Originality: connects functional relations to errors, although annotation methods exist. Potential: clarifies feedback, although descriptions require abstention. Difficulty: little model code, although human calibration is necessary.

Select **matched fixed-slot replacement**. Preserve training targets, final events, padding, slots, and exposed timestamp slots. Match disjoint recent/older nonfinal windows on training popularity; apply identical ordered replacements. Check boundary-transition and title/description coherence using training-only statistics. Report residual imbalance and exclusions; add identity, random-window, and incoherent controls.

Reuse candidates excluding the target and union of original/replacement items. Define changes as perturbed minus original; report target-score change, rank, reciprocal rank, top-10 crossings, ties, and null reasons. Average draws within prefixes, then prefixes within users; bootstrap users within categories and macro-average only when all four categories are available. Separate replacement variability and report small-sample limitations.

Improvement after older-window replacement indicates sensitivity under that intervention, not obsolete intent or isolated positional bias. Preserve adapter contracts, RNG states, one HSTU checkpoint/category, and pinned validation selection. Avoid tuning probes to favorable outcomes.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152; [2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722; [3] https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/; [4] https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html; [5] https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.00786.

idea.description: Extend the existing HSTU diagnosis adapter with paired fixed-slot replacements of recent versus older nonfinal history windows, common-support checks, explicit ranking conventions, and user-cluster uncertainty. Use one frozen trained checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: Deletion probes conflate content removal with position changes. Fixed-slot replacements improve control, but shared inserted items alone do not balance removed content, contextual compatibility, or corruption severity. The revised protocol tests historical dependence while explicitly measuring these limitations; it does not infer satisfied needs, user intent, or held-out performance.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and the host ModelView interfaces. Use view.model in evaluation/inference mode; preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), and predict_score(features, items). Save and restore all module training flags and Python, NumPy, CPU Torch, and CUDA RNG states, including on exceptions. Use a dedicated diagnostic RNG seeded 42.

Use only training histories and training-derived item statistics. Deterministically select up to 32 eligible users per category and two distinct prefix endpoints per user; require at least five occupied events before each training target. Preserve the final event and select two disjoint windows of k=min(2, floor((n-1)/2)) events: the k immediately preceding the final event and the first k occupied events. Record actual window distances. Use five paired replacement draws per prefix, with identical replacement items and ordering for the recent and older variants. Reject unchanged substitutions, duplicate replacement IDs, padding, the target, and items already present in the prefix. Keep sequence length, occupied slots, left padding, and final-event identity fixed. Read features at the greatest nonpadding index, never count-1. Preserve timestamp slots only when exposed by the actual interface; otherwise report timestamp control as unavailable.

For reproducible matching, define item popularity as log1p(training interaction count), standardized within category. Require corresponding original-window popularity values to differ by at most 0.5 standard deviations. Apply replacements within the same tolerance of each corresponding original item, thereby bounding replacement-to-original popularity imbalance. Build title/description TF-IDF features locally without pretrained weights. Estimate smoothed adjacent-item transition scores from training histories only, using a fixed add-one conditional probability. Calculate mean replacement-to-original text cosine similarity and mean log transition probability over all changed edges, including both window boundaries. Accept a paired draw when the recent/older similarity difference is at most 0.10 and their transition-score difference is at most 0.5 training-edge standard deviations; cap attempts at 100 per draw. Report text availability, sparse-transition coverage, matching failures, retained users/prefixes, and residual imbalance. Missing text produces a separately labeled popularity/transition-only analysis, not a fabricated similarity. These thresholds are proposed protocol choices, not established optimal values. Repeat descriptive sensitivity checks using half/double tolerances and k=1; do not select thresholds by favorable rank effects.

Include unchanged-history controls, a nonfinal random-window control using the same replacement bank where feasible, and deliberately low-transition-likelihood replacements as corruption stress tests. These are diagnostic input variants, never independently trained predictors. A remaining recent-versus-older difference reflects sensitivity to different content and locations under the specified controls; it does not isolate absolute position, recency, or any single HSTU component.

For each draw, sample up to 999 unique uniform diagnostic negatives once, excluding the target and the union of items in every compared history. Reuse the exact candidate set across its original and perturbed variants; report candidate count and exclusions. This union exclusion defines a conditional diagnostic catalog and must not modify the pinned benchmark. Report perturbed-minus-original target scores, rank displacement, untruncated reciprocal-rank changes, hit@10 changes, and top-10 entry/exit rates. For g negatives strictly above the target and e exactly tied, report optimistic rank 1+g and pessimistic rank 1+g+e; compute expected reciprocal rank as the mean of 1/r over these e+1 positions and expected hit@10 as the fraction of those positions at or below 10. Do not use target-first stable sorting or reciprocal midrank as a substitute. Report tie frequency and nonfinite-score exclusions. Score differences are checkpoint-scale dependent and should remain category-specific.

Average draws within prefixes and prefixes within users, weighting users equally. Bootstrap whole users within each category using 10,000 resamples and seed 42; report percentile 95% intervals. Keep overlapping prefixes together. Each category probe returns category results and user summaries; only the host aggregation layer computes four-category macro differences, weighting categories equally and resampling within each category independently. Leave macro results null if any category lacks eligible users. Repeat with three independently seeded replacement banks to report Monte Carlo variability separately, without treating banks as additional users. If restricted to the five simulator users per category, report individual effects and leave-one-user-out sensitivity; additional diagnostic training users must not change the simulator cohort. Small-cluster intervals are descriptive and may have poor coverage.

Return metrics and metric_definitions with coverage, exclusions, control checks, uncertainty scope, and null reasons. The interpreter must use measured quantities and distinguish fitted-model sensitivity from validation generalization. Do not adapt thresholds or hypotheses repeatedly to maximize diagnostic significance; training-history optimism and adaptive validation overfitting remain possible.

Preserve all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution, maximum 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch. Count diagnostics against the shared budget. Do not read other trials, hidden tests, or unavailable review/product attributes. Use only fixed macro validation HR@10 for model selection. Any later architecture change must retain HSTU, train exactly one model/checkpoint per category, preserve the diagnostic interfaces, and update the embedded predictor writer consistently.
idea.pseudocode:
save module training flags and all RNG states
try:
    set view.model to eval and enter inference_mode
    build training-only popularity, optional TF-IDF, and transition statistics
    select eligible training users and prefixes deterministically
    for each prefix x, training target y, and replacement draw:
        last = greatest index where x != 0
        choose disjoint older and recent nonfinal windows
        seek one ordered replacement list passing preregistered matching rules
        if matching fails: record exclusion and continue
        construct identity, recent, older, and eligible control variants
        assert identical padding, occupied slots, and final event
        candidates = y plus shared unique negatives excluding union-history items
        for each variant:
            features = view.log2feats(variant)[last]
            scores = view.predict_score(features, candidates)
            compute tie-aware rank bounds, expected reciprocal rank, expected hit@10
        record paired perturbed-minus-original effects and matching diagnostics
    average draws within prefixes and prefixes within users
    bootstrap complete users within category 10,000 times, seed=42
    return metrics, metric_definitions, user summaries, coverage, and null reasons
finally:
    restore module flags and RNG states

host aggregation, only if all four categories have eligible users:
    independently resample users within each category
    average category mean effects equally for each bootstrap replicate
    report macro effects and percentile intervals
report replacement-bank variability separately; never average model predictions

originality.positive: Combines preserved readout, fixed slots, shared ordered replacements, common-support checks, and explicit uncertainty within the supplied HSTU adapter.
originality.negative: Replacement explanations, matching, and clustered inference are established techniques; the contribution is a diagnostic synthesis rather than a new recommendation architecture.

future_potential.positive: Can screen history-dependence hypotheses before expensive retraining and distinguish relatively plausible perturbation effects from obvious corruption sensitivity.
future_potential.negative: Strict matching may retain few users, sparse transitions weaken plausibility checks, and frozen-model sensitivity neither identifies intent nor guarantees validation gains.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses existing feature/scoring interfaces without backbone changes or additional trained predictors.
code_difficulty.negative: Common-support sampling, boundary checks, tie-aware metrics, RNG restoration, and cross-category clustered aggregation require substantially more work than a simple replacement loop.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU with aggregated attention, multiplicative gating, and relative attention biases.
limitations: Does not establish stale-history dependence in the supplied checkpoint or validate this replacement protocol.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias
contributions: Motivates measuring excessive dependence on recent interactions as well as older history.
limitations: Sensitivity to recency alone does not establish useful relevance or transfer to this HSTU implementation.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can yield comparisons inconsistent with full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Shared negatives improve paired comparability but do not remove sampling bias or justify modifying the pinned evaluator.

related_work.title: TREC Product Recommendation Task Definitions
contributions: Distinguishes functional substitute and complement relationships.
limitations: Functional relationships cannot establish ownership, compatibility, current intent, or satisfied needs without additional evidence.

related_work.title: The Out-of-Distribution Problem in Explainability and Search Methods for Feature Importance Explanations
contributions: Explains how replacement choices and distribution shifts can distort feature-importance interpretations.
limitations: Does not supply product-specific matching thresholds or prove that proposed plausibility checks eliminate distribution shift.

related_work.title: Learning Causal Explanations for Recommendation
contributions: Provides precedent for item-replacement explanations that preserve history length.
limitations: Length preservation alone does not establish realistic replacements or causal effects on user preferences.

related_work.title: Computing Information Retrieval Performance Measures Efficiently in the Presence of Tied Scores
contributions: Supports averaging ranking metrics over tied permutations instead of arbitrary ordering.
limitations: Diagnostic tie conventions must remain separate from the host benchmark's fixed implementation.

related_work.title: Cluster Bootstrap Reference
contributions: Supports resampling whole clusters when observations within clusters are dependent.
limitations: Application to overlapping recommendation prefixes requires explicit user-level aggregation; very few users can yield unreliable intervals.

related_work.title: Hierarchical Bootstrap Reference
contributions: Discusses uncertainty estimation for observations with nested dependence.
limitations: Additional replacement draws cannot substitute for independent users or establish population representativeness.

related_work.title: Sequential Recommendation Evaluation Flaws
contributions: Documents how evaluation overlap and temporal leakage can distort sequential-recommendation findings.
limitations: Bootstrap intervals cannot correct training-history optimism, leakage, or adaptive validation selection.
